queries: WITH c AS (SELECT cu.gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count FROM Invoices i JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers cu ON cu.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY cu.gender), s AS (SELECT gender, order_count, order_count * 1.0 / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT gender, order_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT gender, order_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_above_average FROM a WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: An 'invoiced order' is a distinct order that has at least one invoice, so an order with several invoices counts once. Inner joins drop invoices or orders that don't link to a customer.

Each gender value in Customers.gender is its own group. A NULL gender, if any exist, would form its own group and count toward the total and the average. The average share is the mean of the per-gender shares, which equals 1 divided by the number of genders.

alternatives.interpretation: Count invoices rather than distinct orders, so an order with several invoices counts once per invoice.

assumptions.assumption: An 'invoiced order' is an order with at least one invoice, so each order is counted once per gender (COUNT DISTINCT order_id), even if it has several invoices.

The average share is the unweighted mean of the per-gender shares (the total divided by the number of gender groups). Inner joins drop invoices that don't link to an order and customer. A NULL gender, if present, counts as its own group.
Shares are fractions between 0 and 1, left unrounded.

alternatives.interpretation: Count invoices (one per invoice row) instead of distinct orders, so an order with several invoices counts several times.
